xref.title: First Meeting and Kurt Cobain's Death (1994)
xref.body: The band members, including Shirley Manson, met for the first time in London on April 8, 1994, which tragically coincided with the day Kurt Cobain killed himself. Butch Vig, who had produced Nirvana's "Nevermind," received the news during this initial meeting, causing the project to be temporarily put on hold. "They all met up in London on April 8th of 1994. Yeah, that's that's right. They met for the first time the day Kurt Cobain killed himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kurt Cobain's Death Revelation (1994)
xref.body: On April 8, 1994, during his first meeting with Shirley Manson and other future Garbage members in London, Butch Vig received news that Kurt Cobain had killed himself. This tragic event, particularly significant given Vig's role in producing "Nevermind," caused the nascent Garbage project to be put on hold temporarily. "They all met up in London on April 8th of 1994. Yeah, that's that's right. They met for the first time the day Kurt Cobain killed himself."

xref.title: Rejection of Multiple Singers for "The World Is Not Enough" (1999)
xref.body: For "The World Is Not Enough" theme in 1999, David Arnold and the producers considered and rejected a list of prominent artists including Björk, Melanie C of the Spice Girls, Jamiroquai, and Robbie Williams, before ultimately offering the role to Shirley Manson and Garbage. Producers wanted an electronic sound that also retained a big orchestral arrangement. "Calls went out to Bjork, Melanie C of the Spice Girls, Jamira Quye and Robbie Williams and they were all rejected by the producers."

xref.title: Shirley Manson's Discovery
xref.body: Steve Marker discovered Shirley Manson singing with a Scottish band called Angel Fish after seeing her on television, leading to her being tracked down for the new project. "But then it was Steve Marker who turned on a TV and saw a Scottish band called Angel Fish and saw Shirley singing for them."

xref.title: Shirley Manson's Influence
xref.body: Shirley Manson, the Scottish singer drafted into the American band Garbage, has had a notable impact on contemporary artists. Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evanescence, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish, and Lana Del Rey. "Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evan Essence, Katie Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey."

xref.title: Shirley Manson's Initial Audition Failure
xref.body: Shirley Manson initially failed her audition for the band. However, due to her shared musical tastes with the other members, they decided to give her another chance, which she then successfully "nailed." "When Shirley finally did have a chance to audition for the band, she failed. But because she had the same taste in music as the guys, they decided to take a chance anyway."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Stage Performance Motivation
xref.body: Shirley Manson finds stepping on stage to be like a "bolt in the arm," instantly rejuvenating and energizing her. This feeling makes all the "weird things" and difficulties of touring worthwhile, especially when she sees the lit-up faces of the fans enjoying the show. "The minute you step on stage, it's like a bolt in the arm."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
